records.title: Australia Awards Scholarships
records.deadline_display: The 2027 intake round will open on 1 February 2026 9am Australian Eastern Standard Daylight Savings Time (AEDT) and close 30 April 2026 14:00 Australian Eastern Standard Time (AEST).

source.publisher: Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade, Australian Government
source.as_of: Heading of the only dated table on the page: 'Dates for study commencing in 2027'
source.raw_extract: H1: 'Australia Awards opening and closing dates' | H2: 'Dates for study commencing in 2027' | table row -> cell: link 'Bangladesh' (/people-to-people/australia-awards/participating-countries/bangladesh-information-for-intake) | cell '1 February 2026 0900 AEDT' | cell '30 April 2026 1400 AEST' | cell link 'inquiries@australiaawardsbangladesh.org'. The same 1 February 2026 / 30 April 2026 pair appears on every country row except Palau, which reads '30 March 2026 0900 AEDT' and '30 June 2026 1400 AEST'. The linked 'Australia Awards Scholarships' landing page itself publishes no date at all and only links onward to 'Opening and closing dates'.
source.notes: Not a conflicting-source case: two official DFAT pages state the same closing date for the same 2027 intake round. The dedicated dates page gives the country table (Bangladesh: '30 April 2026 1400 AEST'); the DFAT FAQ page states in prose 'The 2027 intake round will open on 1 February 2026 9am Australian Eastern Standard Daylight Savings Time (AEDT) and close 30 April 2026 14:00 Australian Eastern Standard Time (AEST).' These agree exactly. The date is nonetheless in the past as at retrieval (2026-10-05) and no 2028 intake section was observed on the dates page, so per brief section 6 no stale date is written and the date is not shifted forward a year. Note also that the record is not country-specific, so the deadline genuinely varies by country (Palau differs from every other row), which is an additional reason not to write a single date. deadline_semantics is reported as UNKNOWN because no usable value can be written; the underlying provider wording is preserved verbatim above and in raw_extract. Separately: this scholarship is explicitly NOT rolling - the DFAT FAQ answers 'Are applications assessed on a rolling basis?' with 'No. Australia Awards Scholarship applications are not assessed on a rolling basis.'

source.exact_deadline_wording: Applications for Australia Awards Fellowships Round 22 are expected to open in the final quarter of 2026.
source.notes: No closing date exists on the official page for any open or upcoming round. Round 21 closed 16 January 2026 (past). For Round 22 the page gives only an opening expectation of 'the final quarter of 2026' - a quarter, not a month and not a day, and hedged with 'expected'. Per brief sections 5 and 6 this has NOT been converted into a calendar date and no day has been invented. Classified ANNUAL because the page structures the programme as consecutively numbered annual rounds (resources are listed by Round 21, Round 20, Round 19) with no fixed current closing date. Confidence is MEDIUM rather than HIGH because the recurrence is evidenced by round numbering and the next-round statement rather than by an explicit sentence declaring an annual cycle, and because the Round 22 wording is non-binding ('expected'). Important URL correction: the official_source_url in the shard, https://www.dfat.gov.au/people-to-people/australia-awards/australia-awards-fellowships, returns HTTP 404; the live page sits under the duplicated path segment /people-people/ (the same typo exists in DFAT's own site navigation). records.title: CTU Scholarship for Foreign Students - Czech Technical University in Prague

source.raw_extract: H1: 'CTU Scholarships' | The page contains no occurrence of the word 'deadline' and no closing date, intake calendar or application round anywhere in its text. Verbatim from the Master's rules: 'After obtaining the agreement of their faculty and through the International Office at their faculty, foreign students submit an application for a scholarship to the Department of International Relations at the rectorate of CTU. The application should be made on the form that is available on the web pages of the rectorate of CTU.' | 'A scholarship is normally awarded to an individual student for a period of 1 to 2 semesters.' | From the doctoral rules: 'The scholarship is awarded to an individual student for a period of 6-12 months.' | 'Decisions on the award of a scholarship are made by the vice-rector on the basis of a recommendation by the commission of vice-deans for international relations.' | Footer: 'Last changed: 19.09.2025'.
source.notes: This is a genuine absence of evidence rather than insufficient searching. The full live page was retrieved and it describes only a standing administrative procedure (obtain faculty agreement, then apply via the faculty International Office to the Department of International Relations at the rectorate) with no published closing date, no intake calendar and no application round for either the Master's or the doctoral scheme. The absence of the word 'deadline' anywhere on the page is the reason no value is reported. ROLLING was deliberately NOT claimed: the page never says rolling, ongoing or no-fixed-deadline, so asserting ROLLING would be an inference the source does not support. No deadline has been inferred from CTU's general admissions calendar, which is a different programme and barred by brief section 5.

rejected_sources.reason: Application form link surfaced in page text but not fetched; a form carries no deadline and the page itself states no closing date.

source.as_of: Page states 'Updated on 6 August 2026'; the row is explicitly labelled for the 2027 intake
source.raw_extract: H1 area: 'JAPANESE GOVERNMENT (MEXT) SCHOLARSHIPS' | 'Updated on 6 August 2026' | table header row cells: 'Sl. No.' | 'Type' | 'Level' | 'No. of Scholarships' | 'Application Period' | 'Remarks' | Research Student row: link 'Research Student' (Research_Student.html) | 'Research studies (possible to continue to Master's/Ph.D course)' | 'To be announced' | '20 April-15 May,2026' | 'Applications closed for 2027'. For contrast, the sibling rows on the same table read '23 April-25 May,2026' / 'Applications closed for 2027'.
source.notes: This is the most specific official evidence found in the shard: the Embassy's own schedule table gives an explicit application period with a closing day, and the Remarks column states in the provider's own words that the round is closed. The window closed 15 May 2026, which is in the past as at retrieval on 2026-10-05, so per brief section 6 the date is not written and not moved to the 2028 intake. Note that the underlying value was genuinely EXACT (a stated calendar closing date); it is reported as UNKNOWN semantics only because no usable value can be written - the exact provider wording is preserved verbatim in deadline_display and raw_extract so nothing is lost. The generic JASSO/MEXT page at studyinjapan.go.jp was also fetched and corroborates without conflict: 'Recruitment for those arriving in Japan in April 2027 or September/October 2027 is made between April and May of the previous year. First screening is conducted between May and July by the Japanese Embassies or Consulates General. As the application process and specific schedule differ according to the country of your nationality, please inquire the Japanese Embassy or Consulate General in your country for details.' This confirms that country-specific schedules are set by each mission, so the India table is the correct authority for this record. This row's 'To be announced' sits in the No. of Scholarships column, not the Application Period column, and was not misread as a missing date. The linked detail page https://www.in.emb-japan.go.jp/education/japanese_government_scholarships/Research_Student.html returns HTTP 404.
